root_cause: Carbon monoxide poisoning from a faulty gas heater

patient.name: Maya Lindqvist
patient.background: Architecture student, healthy, occasional migraines. Studies late in a basement workshop.

findings.result: Carboxyhemoglobin 28%: CO blocking oxygen on red cells
Pulse oximeter reads 99%, falsely normal (SpO2 artifact)
Mild heart strain, slightly raised troponin
Swollen-looking pale spots in deep brain (globus pallidus)
Mild irritation, no food poisoning toxins (gastritis)
Lactate raised: tissues starving for oxygen
No bleeding or mass on scan (hemorrhage ruled out)

treatments.name: 100% oxygen, consider hyperbaric
treatments.why: High-flow oxygen pushes CO off hemoglobin, cutting its half-life from ~5 hours to ~1, and hyperbaric oxygen protects the brain and heart.
treatments.attending_line: Look at that. Oxygen for oxygen starvation. Someone call the newspapers.

treatments.name: Triptan for migraine
treatments.why: Triptans constrict blood vessels, starving an already oxygen-deprived heart and brain while CO keeps building.
treatments.attending_line: Great, you squeezed the arteries of a heart already gasping. Bold.

treatments.name: Antiemetic and IV fluids
treatments.why: Treating nausea as food poisoning ignores the CO, so tissue hypoxia continues and she may go back to the heater room.
treatments.attending_line: The sushi is innocent. The sushi was always innocent.

treatments.name: Benzodiazepine for anxiety
treatments.why: Sedatives slow breathing, so less fresh air reaches the lungs to wash out CO, and they hide neurological decline.
treatments.attending_line: She's not anxious, she's suffocating politely. Now she's suffocating quietly.

post_mortem: A faulty gas heater in a closed basement workshop filled the air with carbon monoxide, which grabbed Maya's red blood cells and starved her brain and heart of oxygen. The giveaways were the labmate getting dizzy too, symptoms easing outdoors, and a normal pulse oximeter that can't tell CO from oxygen.
